Business E2E map

Who uses Bunkai TMS, the journeys they take end to end, and the feature catalog those journeys cross. Built from the app repo at origin/staging (de0ee80): 39 pages and 88 API route files. Data rules point to business-data-context section ids; endpoint detail belongs to business-api-context.

Overview

Bunkai is used by QA teams organised in workspaces, plus the automation that acts for them. Access is decided twice: by the caller's workspace role (row-level security in the database) and, for a Personal Access Token, by its scopes (checked in the API layer). A browser session holds every scope; its role still limits it.

Role hierarchy

viewer < member < admin < owner. Automation (CI, AI agents) is not a role: it is a member of some role acting through a PAT, recorded on a Run as executor_mode = agent or ci.

Top journeys

  • Execute a Run and file a Bug (journey-execute-run, journey-bug-triage): the product's core loop and the place where evidence is created. Highest risk.
  • Author anchored coverage (journey-author-coverage): story, criteria, ATCs that cannot exist without a criterion.
  • Sign in and set up a workspace (journey-sign-in-onboarding): every other journey starts here; email-dependent steps cannot be automated end to end.
  • Automation through a PAT (journey-headless-automation): the same loop without a browser.
  • Upgrade, export, delete (journey-upgrade-plan, journey-export-data, journey-delete-restore-workspace): money and data leave or change hands.

Persona: workspace owner

System role: workspace_members.role = 'owner' (0001_tenancy.sql). The creator of a workspace is its owner.

Goals: run the team's QA space, pay for it, keep its data portable and decide when it ends.

Exclusive capabilities: export workspace data, delete and restore the workspace (browser session only). Everything an admin can do.

Pain points (messages it can hit): cannot leave while sole owner (sole_owner, 45213); a fourth project on the free plan is refused by the project limit; an export link answers "expired" after 7 days (45803).

Journeys: sign-in-onboarding, invite-join, upgrade-plan, export-data, delete-restore-workspace, plus every member journey.

Test account: none dedicated. The QA repo declares only STAGING_USER_EMAIL / LOCAL_USER_EMAIL; an owner account needs its own key (for example STAGING_OWNER_EMAIL).

Persona: workspace admin (QA lead)

System role: admin; checked by bunkai_is_workspace_admin.

Goals: bring people into the team with the right role, see seats and usage, upgrade the plan, connect a project to Jira.

Capabilities beyond a member: invite and revoke (viewer, member, admin; never owner), billing overview and checkout, tracker settings, close any Test Plan.

Pain points: an invite to an email that is already an active member is refused; billing is invisible to non-admins (the API answers 404, never 403).

Journeys: invite-join, upgrade-plan, plus every member journey.

Test account: none dedicated; needs its own key.

Persona: QA engineer (member)

System role: member; writes pass bunkai_can_write_workspace.

Goals: turn stories into anchored ATCs, chain them into Tests, execute Runs, file Bugs with evidence, track a plan.

Pain points (messages it can hit): "Please give a reason of at least 3 characters" when aborting; "No environments configured" when a project has no environment; a story cannot move to ready to test without a criterion (ac_required_for_ready_to_test); an ATC chained in a Test cannot be deleted; a closed Run refuses marks.

Journeys: author-coverage, jira-import, build-test, execute-run, bug-triage, test-plan, reporting.

Test account: STAGING_USER_EMAIL / LOCAL_USER_EMAIL (the only role covered today; its exact role on staging was not verified).

Persona: viewer (stakeholder)

System role: viewer.

Goals: follow coverage, Runs and Bugs without changing them (developers, product people).

Behaviour: sees everything in the workspace; write controls are hidden (the runner shows no Abort, Finish or mark controls) and every write is refused by RLS or the RPC role gate. A Test Plan creator who was demoted to viewer can no longer close it.

Journeys: reporting, sign-in.

Test account: none; needed for every negative permission case.

Persona: CI pipeline or AI agent

System identity: a user's Personal Access Token (Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…); its Runs carry executor_mode agent or ci.

Goals: read and write ATCs, start Runs, mark steps and finish them from a pipeline.

Rules: the token's owner role still applies; scopes narrow it further; default scopes are atc:read, atc:write, run:execute; workspace:admin is never default. Several endpoints refuse a PAT entirely (tokens, data export, workspace delete and restore, membership, active workspace).

Pain points: a uniform 401 for any token problem (no hint whether it was revoked, expired or malformed); a missing scope answers 403.

Journeys: headless-automation.

Journey: sign in and set up a workspace

Entry: /login (or any protected page, which redirects to /login?next=…).

  1. Type an email; the app asks whether the account exists and is confirmed.
  2. Existing account: password. New account: password, then a 6 to 8 digit code sent by email. Alternatives: magic link, GitHub or Google OAuth. (Details: infra-context section architecture.)
  3. With no active membership, /home, /projects and /projects/new redirect to /onboarding.
  4. Create the workspace (name, slug): the user becomes owner on the free plan (business-data-context flow-workspace-bootstrap).
  5. Create the first project at /projects/new; Staging and Production environments are seeded.

Branches and failures: wrong password (uniform error); signup for an existing email (409); OTP rate limit (429); expired or wrong code (401); slug taken or reserved; a fourth project on the free plan.

External-dependency steps: the signup code, the magic link and OAuth consent need a real mailbox or provider and are not automatable end to end; headless tests sign in through POST /api/v1/auth/signin.

Journey: invite a teammate, join, leave

  1. An admin or owner opens the workspace members page and invites an email with a role.
  2. The app shows the accept link once; no email is sent, so the admin shares it.
  3. The invitee opens /invites/accept, signs in with the same email and accepts; the membership becomes active and the workspace appears in their switcher.
  4. Later, any member can leave the workspace from settings.

Failures: invite expired, revoked or already accepted (each its own 409 message); email mismatch; inviting an existing member; leaving as sole owner or from one's only workspace. Data: business-data-context flow-invite, state-workspace-member.

Journey: author anchored coverage

Entry: the project page (/projects/[projectSlug]), whose explorer shows the module tree.

  1. Create or rename modules and sub-modules (6 levels at most); move or archive them.
  2. Create a user story in a module; add and reorder acceptance criteria.
  3. Mark the story ready to test (needs at least one active criterion).
  4. Create an ATC at atcs/new: title, layer (UI, API, Unit), optional technique and priority, tags, steps, assertions, and at least one criterion of the story.
  5. Search, duplicate, edit or export ATCs (CSV export from the project page). The ATC page shows "Used in N tests".

Failures: saving without a criterion; title too short; too many tags; deleting a story that still has ATCs; deleting an ATC that a Test chains. Data: business-data-context flow-authoring, entity-atc.

Journey: import stories from Jira

  1. From the project page, open "Import from Jira" and give the source query.
  2. The import runs in the background; the dialog polls its status.
  3. Imported stories land as draft with their Jira key; a re-import updates instead of duplicating.

Failures: an import already running for the project (409 import_in_progress); Jira credentials not configured on the deployment (the job fails); per-issue errors listed on the job. External dependency: Jira Cloud. Data: flow-jira-import.

Journey: build a Test

  1. At tests/new, name the Test and pick ATCs in order (the same ATC may appear more than once).
  2. Open the Test: its chain shows each ATC expanded with steps and assertions.
  3. Reorder the chain, and tag it (smoke, sanity, regression or custom); filter Tests by tag.

Failures: an ATC outside the workspace; a reorder that adds or removes ATCs, or that races another edit (version conflict).

Journey: execute a Run

Entry: a Test's page, "Start run". Highest-risk journey: it creates the evidence everything else reports on.

  1. Pick an environment; the Run starts and the app routes to runs/[runId] with every step pending.
  2. Mark each step passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note. A second viewer sees marks live (Supabase Realtime).
  3. Finish with a verdict (passed or failed), or abort with a reason of 3 to 500 characters. Remaining pending steps become skipped.
  4. From a finished Run, compare it with the previous finished Run of the same Test and environment (runs/[runId]/compare).

Branches and failures: no environment configured; a Test with no executable steps; marking or finishing a Run that another person already ended (first terminal action wins); a Run left idle for 4 hours is aborted by the system and its starter is notified; viewers get a read-only runner.

Silent risk: results never update atcs.status; coverage reads Runs. Data: business-data-context flow-run-execution, state-run.

Journey: file and triage a Bug

  1. In the runner, on a failed step, "Report bug" opens the bug form pre-linked to the Run, step and ATC, with the ATC's module read-only. It stays available after the Run has ended (a failure that happened stays reportable). A Bug can also be filed standalone from the Bug Reports page.
  2. Fill title, severity (P1 to P4) and module.
  3. On bugs/[bugId], the detail shows the origin ("Failed at step N of …", or "Filed manually").
  4. Assign it to a member; move it forward: open → in progress → resolved → closed.
  5. The assignee and the people involved get notifications.

Failures: skipping a status or moving backwards; assigning someone who is not an eligible member; a viewer trying to triage. Data: flow-bug-filing, state-bug.

Journey: plan, track and close a test effort

  1. Create a Test Plan with a name and a goal (plans).
  2. Add Tests whose whole chain belongs to the project; remove them as needed.
  3. Follow progress: each member Test's latest Run outcome and the passed percentage, in the list and on the plan page.
  4. Close with a verdict and an optional summary; progress is frozen. Reopen if needed.

Failures: duplicate plan name; a Test spanning several projects; editing a closed plan; a member who is not the creator trying to close it. Data: flow-test-plan.

Journey: follow quality

  • Home: welcome summary, active Runs, open Bugs, workspace coverage, recent projects and activity.
  • Traceability: one story's chain criterion → ATC → Test → Run → Bug, filterable by module.
  • Metrics: coverage (with a "not run" filter), recovery cycles and the defect heatmap.
  • Test Runs: the project's Runs with pass and fail totals; a Test's own run history.
  • Milestones: goals with a target date.
  • Activity: the workspace audit stream.
  • Search (⌘K) across ATCs, Tests, projects, modules, Bugs and Runs; saved views on traceability, run history, Bugs and the workbench.

Journey: automation through a PAT

  1. Obtain a token once: POST /api/v1/auth/signin returns a session and a fresh PAT, or a person creates one under Settings → Tokens.
  2. Call the API with Authorization: Bearer: read and write ATCs (atc:read, atc:write), start a Run with executor_mode agent or ci, mark steps and finish (run:execute).
  3. Send an Idempotency-Key when starting a Run, creating a Test or adding Tests to a plan (required on those): a retried call replays the first answer instead of writing twice.

Failures: uniform 401 for an invalid, expired or revoked token; 403 for a missing scope; a token bound to workspace A refused in workspace B; endpoints that accept a browser session only.

Journey: upgrade to the paid plan

Money changes hands here.

  1. An admin or owner opens Settings → Billing: plan, seats used, projects and oldest-run age against the plan limits.
  2. "Upgrade" (settings/billing/upgrade) starts a Stripe Checkout session and redirects to Stripe.
  3. After payment Stripe returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1; the plan changes when Stripe's webhook confirms payment, which can lag the redirect.
  4. The checkout can be cancelled, which releases the one-open-checkout lock.

Failures: a second checkout while one is open; payment failed or session expired (plan unchanged). External dependency: Stripe's hosted page is not automatable end to end without Stripe test mode. Data: flow-billing-upgrade.

Journey: export workspace data

  1. The owner opens Settings → Data export (hidden for other roles) and requests an export.
  2. The archive is built in the background; the page shows its status.
  3. Download it within 7 days.

Failures: a second request while one is in flight; downloading before it is ready or after it expired. Data: flow-workspace-export.

Journey: delete and restore a workspace

Data is destroyed here, irreversibly after 30 days.

  1. The owner deletes the workspace from settings. Every member loses access at once and receives an email.
  2. Within 30 days, the owner follows the emailed link to /workspaces/[id]/restore and restores it.
  3. After 30 days the daily purge removes the data for good.

Failures: a non-owner trying to delete; a double submit; restoring a workspace that is not deleted. Data: flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace.

Cross-feature: notifications

Bugs and Runs produce events; notifications show them in an inbox (read one or read all); settings decide the email digest. A run event is not sent to the person who ended the Run interactively. The in-app preference toggle is stored but not applied (see business-data-context flow-notifications); "mentions" is shown and locked.

Cross-feature: editing an ATC that is already in use

An ATC edit reaches every Test that chains it immediately (Tests hold references), never reaches a Run already started (Runs hold a snapshot), and Run compare still pairs steps across the edit through the ATC occurrence and the exact step text. Testing an edit means checking three features at once: ATC library, Tests and Runs.

Cross-feature: traceability and coverage

The traceability view and coverage are read across authoring, Tests, Runs and Bugs. Coverage counts an ATC as executed only when its latest Run result is passed or failed; an aborted or skipped Run leaves its criteria "not run". A change in any of the four features can move these numbers.

API endpoint inventory

Endpoint groups live in business-api-context, not here. 88 route files on origin/staging group as: auth, tokens and identity (auth/*, me, tokens); workspaces, members, invites, billing, export, notifications; projects, environments, modules, user stories, criteria; ATCs; Tests; Runs; Bugs; Test Plans and milestones; reports (coverage, traceability, recovery cycles, heatmap, run report, search, saved views); imports; platform (health, OpenAPI, billing webhook, digest cron).

Feature flags and WIP

No feature flag is read by the app: the feature_flags table exists but no code reads it, and no FEATURE_ / ENABLE_ / BETA_ variable gates behaviour (the only FEATURE_ match is a marketing list on the login page). Unfinished work is signalled by "coming soon" navigation entries (see ui-inventory) and by the in-development features in feature-wip.
